spec.title: Rows read per second by the whole group
spec.description: What the group reads from Kafka and writes to Postgres, summed over its members. The load is a steady 2000/s, so a healthy group sits near 2000 after warm-up. A dip to 0 is a pause: the group read nothing. Look for the dip at the scenario time (see runs.tsv) and compare eager (roundRobin) with cooperativeSticky. Surprising: a dip when nothing happened to the group, or no dip at all in an eager run. A restarted member's counter starts again at 0, rate() handles that.

spec.title: Group lag (topic k8-events)
spec.description: Records produced but not yet committed by the group (kafka-exporter). It grows while the group is paused and falls when it catches up after the pause. Surprising: lag that never falls back after the scenario. The exporter scrape is 1 s but it only refreshes about every few seconds, so short pauses look smoothed.

spec.title: Ingest p99 latency (k6)
spec.description: Latency of POST /v1/events seen by k6. The API only waits for Kafka, not for the consumers, so it should stay flat during any rebalance. Surprising: a latency rise at the scenario time. Native-histogram form, no _bucket series.

spec.title: Accepted vs offered (k6)
spec.description: 202 answers per second against all answers per second. They should both be 2000. A gap means the API shed load, which would hide the consumer effect behind an API problem.

spec.title: Event freshness p99
spec.description: Time from the API receiving an event to its row being committed (histogram of ep_event_freshness_seconds). It rises when the group pauses because events wait in Kafka. Surprising: a high value before the scenario acts. Only counts rows the sink wrote, so it has no data while nothing is written.

spec.title: Run phase
spec.description: 0 steady, 1 the scenario is acting on the group, 2 after it, -1 no run (textfile ep_k8_phase written by run.sh). Added by K8; it only exists while run.sh runs. Use it to line up the other panels with the scenario time.

spec.title: Group members
spec.description: Members the coordinator knows (kafka_consumergroup_members). Counts up in s1, down in s2, and in s3 it drops by one after the session timeout (6 s) and comes back after the resume. Surprising: s3 not dropping, which would mean the frozen member kept its session.

spec.title: Partitions owned per consumer
spec.description: ep_consumer_assigned_partitions of each consumer-sink (ports 8001-8003). A settled group owns 6 in total. Eager rebalancing sends every member to 0 for a moment, cooperative should not. Surprising: a member at 0 in a cooperative run that only gains partitions.

spec.title: Revoke callbacks per consumer (cumulative)
spec.description: ep_consumer_revokes_total, ADDED BY K8. Counts the times the rebalance took partitions away from a member. Steps up at each rebalance. A cooperative run that only adds members should show few or no revokes on the old member.

spec.title: Partitions revoked per consumer (cumulative)
spec.description: ep_consumer_partitions_revoked_total, ADDED BY K8. How many partitions were taken from each member in total. Eager revokes everything the member owns every time; cooperative only the partitions that move. This is the cleanest eager vs cooperative signal.

spec.title: Revoke to assign gap per consumer (cumulative s)
spec.description: ep_consumer_rebalance_gap_seconds_sum, ADDED BY K8. Seconds between the revoke callback and the next assign callback inside one member. It misses the time the group spent before the revoke callback (waiting for all members to rejoin), so it understates the real pause; the rows-read panel shows the real one.

spec.title: Rows read per second by consumer
spec.description: Who is reading. Shows the work move between members after the scenario: new members start reading in s1, the stopped one disappears in s2, the frozen one goes quiet in s3.

spec.title: Chunk processing p99
spec.description: Whole chunk: parse, write, commit (ep_consumer_batch_processing_seconds). Normal chunks are far below 1 s. In s4 the slow chunk is 12 s, above the 8 s rebalance timeout, so a spike here marks the stall. The top histogram bucket is 30 s.

spec.title: Offset commit errors (cumulative)
spec.description: ep_consumer_commit_errors_total. A commit during or after a rebalance can fail because the member no longer owns the partition. Rows already written are then read again by the new owner, which is how duplicates appear. Surprising: commit errors in a run where nobody was revoked.

spec.title: Assign callbacks per consumer (cumulative)
spec.description: ep_consumer_rebalances_total: assignments received (group joins). It counts the first join too, so a member that never rebalanced shows 1.

spec.title: Consumer CPU (pinned cores)
spec.description: Busy share of the cores the consumers are pinned to (1 and 7). The third consumer shares core 1 with the first. Keep it under about 70% so CPU contention does not look like a rebalance effect.

spec.title: Process CPU per consumer
spec.description: CPU seconds per second used by each consumer-sink process. 1.0 is one full core.

spec.title: Broker cores busy
spec.description: Busy share of the broker cores (2, 8, 3, 9). Rebalances load the group coordinator broker a little; a high value here would be a different problem.

spec.title: Consumer event-loop lag
spec.description: nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds of each consumer. A frozen (SIGSTOP) process stops answering, so its line has a hole in s3. Surprising: large lag in the other cells, which would mean the consumer was starved.

spec.title: Postgres pool waiting per consumer
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_waiting: callers waiting for a pool connection. Should stay 0: every consumer handles one partition at a time and the pool has 5.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations
spec.description: Must be 0 in a measured run. Dropped iterations mean k6 could not start requests on time, so the offered load was not the planned one: discard that run.

spec.title: k6 non-202 answers
spec.description: Answers that are not 202. Must be 0: an API error means events that cannot be expected in Postgres.

spec.title: k6 cores busy
spec.description: Generator headroom (cores 4 and 10). Keep under about 70%.

spec.title: API cores busy
spec.description: Busy share of the API cores (0 and 6). The API must not be the bottleneck at 2000 req/s (the knee is about 7500).

spec.title: Monitoring and Postgres cores busy
spec.description: Busy share of cores 5 and 11, which also run Postgres. A saturated Postgres would slow every consumer in the same way and hide the rebalance effect.

spec.title: API failed Kafka publishes
spec.description: ep_kafka_messages_failed_total rate of the API. Must be 0: a failed publish would be an event k6 counted as accepted but Kafka never got.
